channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Structured exercise interventions and survival outcomes in patients with cancer: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 RCTs (n=3828 for OS) found structured exercise associated with significant improvements in overall survival (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.65-0.92), disease-free survival (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72-0.95), all-cause mortality (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.97), and cancer-specific mortality (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57-0.96). Evidence certainty was moderate for key outcomes.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effects of Somatosensory Interventions on Sensory, Motor, and Balance Functions in Individuals with Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of nine RCTs (N=330) found that somatosensory interventions significantly improved Berg Balance Scale scores in stroke patients compared to conventional therapy, though no significant effects were observed for upper limb motor function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Percutaneous Electrolysis for the Management of Musculoskeletal Disorders. A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found very low-certainty evidence that adding percutaneous electrolysis (PNE) to therapeutic exercise was not superior to sham or exercise alone for pain or function in tendinopathies. Low-certainty evidence suggested PNE plus exercise might reduce short-to-medium term pain more than dry needling plus exercise in tendinopathy but not in myofascial pain syndrome.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Short-Term Effects of Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy in Addition to Physiotherapy on Spasticity, Walking Performance, and Quality of Life in Chronic Stroke: A Sham-Controlled Randomized Trial.
item.description: A sham-controlled randomized trial (n=85) found that adding 4 weeks of radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT) to physiotherapy significantly improved spasticity (MAS mean difference -0.56, 95% CI -0.77 to -0.35), walking performance (10MWT -1.41 s), motor function (FMA-LE 4.42), and quality of life (SS-QOL 11.73) in chronic stroke patients with plantar flexor spasticity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Do blood flow restriction exercises offer additional benefits when compared to conventional exercises in musculoskeletal rehabilitation? A systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 45 RCTs (n=1652) found low-certainty evidence that low-load exercise with blood flow restriction (LLE-BFR) was superior to low-load exercise (LLE) for muscle strength (SMD=0.82) and disability (SMD=0.63). Moderate-certainty evidence showed no clear difference between LLE-BFR and high-load exercise (HLE) for muscle strength (SMD=0.08). Pain reductions for LLE-BFR were small and not clinically meaningful.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Optimal exercise dose in adults with chronic low back pain disorders: systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of 239 trials found that low-to-moderate doses of exercise were associated with short-term, clinically meaningful improvements in disability and pain intensity for adults with chronic low back pain, with limited additional benefit at higher exposure. Optimal doses were model-predicted as 4 sessions/week, 25 min/session over 13 weeks for disability, and 3 sessions/week, 30 min/session over 8 weeks for pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise-only interventions and exercise-based multidomain lifestyle interventions to promote cognitive function in older adults without dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 227 studies found that exercise-only interventions significantly improved executive functions, memory, and processing speed in older adults without dementia compared to control. Exercise-plus interventions (exercise combined with other lifestyle interventions, most commonly cognitive training) were significantly better than control for memory, and better than exercise-only for executive functions and processing speed.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of TENS, NMES, and Combination Therapy on Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain and Function After Stroke.
item.description: A randomized study (n=60) found that combined TENS+NMES significantly reduced hemiplegic shoulder pain and SPADI scores compared to TENS alone in acute/subacute stroke patients, but did not improve upper extremity motor function, spasticity, or ADL.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical Exercise Reduces Fall-Related Outcomes Among People With Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (n=1536) found that physical exercise significantly reduced the number of falls by 39% (IRR = 0.61, 95% CI = [0.47, 0.78]) in people with stroke, with balance training and cognitive components being most effective, particularly for those in the chronic stage with mild to moderate disability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Calf Injuries: An Anatomy-Based Approach to Diagnosis, Management and Return to Sport.
item.description: A review highlights that anatomical characterization of calf muscle injuries, including gastrocnemius-soleus, is useful for understanding heterogeneity, but clinical management and return-to-sport decisions should prioritize progressive, criteria-based loading over isolated imaging findings.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Strength training as an effective strategy for injury prevention and performance enhancement in team sports: a scoping review
item.description: A scoping review of 17 RCTs (n=20-652 athletes, mean age 12.7-25.8 years) found that structured strength training was associated with improvements in injury-related outcomes (lower incidence of hamstring strains, groin injuries, overall injuries) and performance outcomes (sprint speed, jump height, muscular strength/endurance) in team-sport athletes.
item.author: Sport Sci Health

item.title: CPG | Interventions for the Management of Acute and Chronic Low Back Pain: Revision 2021
item.description: The APTA Academy of Orthopaedic Physical Therapy published a 2021 revision of its clinical practice guideline for the management of acute and chronic low back pain, providing updated recommendations for physical therapy interventions, including specific considerations for older adults and postoperative patients.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Association Between Admission Serum Albumin and Short-Term Functional Improvement During Inpatient Rehabilitation After Cervical Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A single-center retrospective cohort study of 106 cervical traumatic spinal cord injury patients found that higher serum albumin at rehabilitation admission was associated with greater short-term functional improvement in basic ADL (aOR 1.23 per 1-g/L increase; 95% CI, 1.08-1.41; P=0.002).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Age, resilience, social support, and health literacy as predictors of functional ability in people with spinal cord injury: a 6-month follow-up study.
item.description: A 6-month follow-up study (N=367) on traumatic spinal cord injury patients found that younger age (β = -0.02; p = 0.028), higher resilience (β = 0.22; p < 0.001), and higher health literacy (β = 0.32; p = 0.001) were significant independent predictors of greater functional ability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Priorities and design principles for a mobile health (mHealth) application to support self-management of post-stroke aphasia: experience gathering and prioritisation within an experience-based co-design approach.
item.description: An experience-based co-design study, involving 13 people with aphasia, 8 significant others, and 10 health professionals, identified five design principles for a mobile health (mHealth) application to support self-management of post-stroke aphasia. Principles include connecting users with clinicians and community, linking goals to outcomes, visual progress tracking, and customizability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A sex-positive approach to sexual rehabilitation after SCI: exploring women's sexual experiences using participatory action research.
item.description: A participatory action research study involving 15 Canadian women with spinal cord injury (SCI) explored their sexual experiences using a sex-positive approach. Three main themes emerged: relationship with the self, changes in the body, and intimacy with partners, highlighting the importance of self-confidence, self-exploration, and incorporating assistive devices.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Cerebellar Theta-Burst Stimulation Induces Distinct Functional Connectivity Patterns in Post-Stroke Aphasia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial found that cerebellar continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) did not confer significant overall language recovery benefit in subacute post-stroke aphasia (PSA) patients, but selectively improved repetition performance (P = .034). Functional connectivity changes between right cerebellar Crus I and temporo-occipital regions were associated with behavioral outcomes, showing marked inter-individual variability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of Music-Based Interventions in Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of nine studies found music-based interventions in cardiac rehabilitation primarily improved psychological outcomes, motivation, exercise adherence, and functional performance, serving as supportive adjuncts rather than directly affecting cardiovascular parameters.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: REmotely monitored, Mobile health-supported Multidomain Rehabilitation with High Intensity Interval Training for COVID-19 (REMM-HIIT-CoV): Trial Design and Rationale.
item.description: This multicenter, single-blinded RCT (n=140) will evaluate a 12-week remotely monitored, mobile health-supported multidomain rehabilitation program with HIIT in community-dwelling adults post-COVID-19 hospitalization. The primary outcome is 6-minute walk distance at 3 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: From evidence to action: a global call to advance sleep health in sport
item.description: This editorial calls for advancing sleep health in sport, presenting evidence-based practices to address misalignments between high-performance environments and healthy sleep/circadian biology. It emphasizes that sleep health is a multidimensional construct crucial for athlete performance.
item.author: BJSM
